result.title: Whose Values Are Generated? Measuring Visual Value Leakage in Multilingual Text-to-Image Generation
result.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) systems serve users across languages and cultural contexts. However, evaluations of cultural representation focus mainly on recognizable elements such as landmarks, clothing, and activities, overlooking the cultural values that generated images convey. To bridge this gap, we introduce VisionValueBench, a multilingual benchmark that operationalizes six of Hofstede's cultural value dimensions (e.g., individualism versus collectivism) to investigate how T2I systems frame neutral social situations through a particular cultural orientation. We find that value-neutral prompts, which admit diverse cultural interpretations, nonetheless yield images that favor particular value orientations, a phenomenon we call visual value leakage. We evaluate prompts varying in language and geographic cues across 960 social scenarios and six T2I configurations. Generated images consistently favor the same value orientations across all six dimensions, for example, equality over hierarchy (low power distance), individual autonomy over group obligation (individualism), and enjoyment over restraint (indulgence). Prompt language has limited influence on these orientations, whereas geographic cues shift some dimensions toward the associated cultural values while largely preserving the prevailing orientations. These findings reveal substantial homogeneity in the cultural values conveyed by T2I systems worldwide.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 VisionValueBench，一个多语言基准，用 Hofstede 的六个文化价值维度检验 T2I 系统在价值中立的社会场景提示下是否输出偏向特定价值取向的图像，即「视觉价值泄漏」，并比较提示语言与地理线索的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究重点是图像生成中的文化价值偏向与提示语言效应，不涉及 VLM 的推理状态表示、视觉证据筛选、动态计算或停止决策，也未提供可迁移到 LVR 的方法或评价线索。
